s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital vascular and soft tissue anomalies with overgrowth and malformations
salient_findings: Multiple soft masses on the anterior upper chest, abdomen, and right arm
Large port-wine–colored capillary malformation on the trunk
Hypertrophy of the left thigh, overgrowth of both feet, and syndactyly of the toes
Dilated, tortuous veins over the chest and left leg
Cystic, septated masses consistent with lymphangiomas on MRI
key_facts: 20-month-old girl
Congenital soft-tissue masses and cutaneous vascular lesions
Multiple soft masses on the anterior upper chest, abdomen, and right arm
Large port-wine–colored capillary malformation on the trunk
Hypertrophy of the left thigh
Overgrowth of both feet
Syndactyly of the second and third toes on the right
Dilated, tortuous veins over the chest and left leg
No facial dysmorphism
No cardiac murmur
No organomegaly
Full muscle strength
Intact reflexes
Normal developmental milestones and growth parameters
Born by cesarean delivery to a nonconsanguineous couple
Pregnancy notable for fetal malformations
Two older siblings healthy
Skeletal survey demonstrated fused toes and soft-tissue hypertrophy
MRI revealed extensive cystic, septated, high–T2-signal masses consistent with lymphangiomas
Liver, kidneys, and pancreas appeared normal aside from hemangiomas

shortlist.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by congenital vascular malformations, soft tissue and bone hypertrophy, which matches the patient's presentation of port-wine stains, soft tissue masses, and limb overgrowth

shortlist.label: CLOVES syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Involves congenital lipomatous overgrowth, vascular malformations, epidermal nevi, and skeletal anomalies, aligning with the patient's clinical features of soft tissue masses, vascular lesions, and skeletal abnormalities

shortlist.label: Parkes Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by congenital vascular malformations and soft tissue hypertrophy, similar to the patient's presentation, with an emphasis on the presence of arteriovenous malformations

shortlist.label: Proteus syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Involves congenital malformations and overgrowth of multiple tissues, which could explain the patient's diverse clinical features including soft tissue masses, vascular lesions, and skeletal anomalies

shortlist.label: Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Combines features of Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome with those of Parkes Weber syndrome, including arteriovenous malformations, which could account for the patient's complex vascular and soft tissue anomalies

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of congenital soft-tissue masses, cutaneous vascular lesions, port-wine–colored capillary malformation, and hypertrophy of the left thigh are consistent with Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome. The presence of lymphangiomas and hemangiomas also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: CLOVES syndrome
rejected.why: CLOVES syndrome typically presents with more severe and complex congenital anomalies, including spinal and skeletal abnormalities, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Parkes Weber syndrome
rejected.why: Parkes Weber syndrome is characterized by the presence of a capillary malformation, arteriovenous malformation, and soft-tissue hypertrophy, but the patient's lymphangiomas and hemangiomas are more suggestive of Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome.

rejected.label: Proteus syndrome
rejected.why: Proteus syndrome is a highly variable disorder that can present with a wide range of congenital anomalies, but the patient's specific findings are more consistent with Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome.

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome is not a recognized medical term, and the patient's presentation is more consistent with Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome.
